note: Generated from the matrix specification tables; do not edit by hand. Matrix IDs carry the MATRIX: prefix in other documents.

categories.name: Agents inside an editor or IDE
categories.description: Operate alongside the developer in the coding environment, gathering context, editing files, and running checks.

categories.name: Terminal or command-line agents
categories.description: Act on a repository through files, shell commands, and development tools, with a terminal interface.

categories.name: Background or cloud coding agents
categories.description: Receive delegated tasks, work in a separate environment, and return changes for review.

categories.name: Integrated application builders
categories.description: Combine natural-language app creation with a managed workspace, previews, services, and deployment.

categories.name: Specialized development agents
categories.description: Focus on an activity such as code review, testing, failure investigation, or security fixes.

categories.name: Agent orchestration frameworks
categories.description: Provide programming components for building agents and coordinating tools, roles, and interactions.

categories.name: Specification-driven workflow toolkits
categories.description: Provide a structured process for requirements, planning, task decomposition, implementation, and verification using a coding agent.

features.name: Persistent project instructions
features.capability: Save coding standards, security rules, and test commands for use across tasks.
features.examine: Supported instruction formats, discovery rules, precedence, persistence, and scope.

features.name: Planning before implementation
features.capability: Produce a developer-reviewable plan before changing code.
features.examine: Planning modes, review steps, and documented transition from planning to implementation. Distinguish optional planning from a required approval gate.

features.name: Requirements traceability
features.capability: Connect a requirement to implementation and verification evidence.
features.examine: Explicit linking of requirements, tasks, changes, and checks. A plan or task list alone does not establish traceability.

features.name: Codebase context gathering
features.capability: Locate and inspect relevant existing code without requiring all context to be supplied manually.
features.examine: Repository search, indexing, file inspection, context selection, and documented limits.

features.name: Coordinated changes across files
features.capability: Update related code, configuration, and tests together.
features.examine: Multi-file editing support, relevant modes, and documented restrictions.

features.name: Execution and feedback
features.capability: Run builds or tests, inspect failures, and revise work based on results.
features.examine: Command and test execution, access to results, and documented feedback or revision loops. Do not infer successful defect correction.

features.name: Tool and permission restrictions
features.capability: Limit commands, files, external services, or network destinations accessible to the agent.
features.examine: Allow/deny controls and their command, filesystem, service, and network coverage. Distinguish approval prompts from access restrictions.

features.name: Execution isolation
features.capability: Run agent actions within an environment with enforced boundaries.
features.examine: Documented sandbox mechanisms, defaults, filesystem/network boundaries, platform restrictions, and exceptions. A branch or Git worktree alone does not establish isolation.

features.name: Secrets handling
features.capability: Supply credentials through a supported mechanism without placing them in prompts, generated code, or committed files.
features.examine: Credential delivery, storage, redaction, exposure boundaries, and documented limits. Product sign-in alone does not establish safe handling of application secrets.

features.name: Approval checkpoints
features.capability: Require developer approval before selected actions.
features.examine: Actions requiring approval, defaults, configuration, bypasses, and mode-specific exceptions.

features.name: Inspection and intervention
features.capability: View progress, inspect proposed changes, redirect work, and stop the agent.
features.examine: Progress and diff views, steering and cancellation controls, and limits on interrupting ongoing actions. Record each subcapability separately.

features.name: Change recovery
features.capability: Discard or revert code changes with clear limits on recovery coverage.
features.examine: Checkpoints, undo, restore, or Git-based recovery; coverage of files, shell effects, external actions, and deployed resources.

features.name: Reusable skills and task workflows
features.capability: Package, share, version, and invoke recurring procedures.
features.examine: Native formats, discovery and invocation rules, sharing mechanisms, and documented requirements. Assess the mechanism without adding a skill to the profile.

features.name: External tool integration
features.capability: Connect to issue trackers, documentation, databases, or other systems through MCP or another interface.
features.examine: Supported interfaces or protocols, authentication, configuration, permission controls, and limits. Assess native integration support without connecting a service.

features.name: Repository and CI/CD integration
features.capability: Work with branches, pull requests, automated checks, and deployment workflows.
features.examine: Explicit support for each stage. Branch or pull-request support alone does not establish a complete CI/CD or deployment pipeline.

features.name: Action logs and audit trail
features.capability: Inspect and export tool calls, commands, results, and changes associated with a task.
features.examine: Recorded events, run association, export formats, retention, and integrity guarantees where documented. Distinguish chat history from an audit trail.

features.name: Usage and cost visibility
features.capability: Obtain task-level token usage, charges, or another clearly defined usage measure.
features.examine: Units, granularity, reporting and estimation methods. Distinguish context usage, tokens, request allowances, and monetary charges.

features.name: Execution limits
features.capability: Set time, iteration, or spending limits to contain runaway work.
features.examine: Supported limits, defaults, scope, overrides, and documented enforcement. Distinguish hard limits from estimates, warnings, and instruction-based requests.

statuses.name: Built in
statuses.meaning: Official documentation establishes native support within the profile. A native feature may still require an optional setting; record activation separately.

statuses.name: Configuration or extension required
statuses.meaning: Official documentation establishes support through an additional integration or separately assembled configuration outside the native capability assessed. Identify the dependency and whether it is excluded from the profile.

statuses.name: Custom implementation required
statuses.meaning: Documentation explicitly describes implementation work needed to supply the capability. Identify the code and maintenance responsibility. Do not infer this status from a documentation gap.

statuses.name: Unavailable
statuses.meaning: Official documentation explicitly establishes that the capability is unsupported within the assessed profile.

statuses.name: Not established from documentation
statuses.meaning: Reviewed sources are silent, ambiguous, conflicting, or insufficient to establish support or absence.
